name: Brass compass
role: Captain Livé’s separate navigation inventory prop
dimension_contract: dimensions_m describes the flat, dial-up engine resting pose. The reference images deliberately show the same object upright to expose its dial. Correct the reconstruction orientation before measuring the final mesh. The illustration is a reconstruction reference, not a metrically exact CAD model.

design.description: One shallow round brass compass with a broad worn bezel, clear slightly domed glass, an ivory dial, a dark eight-point compass rose, one red/ivory magnetic needle and a central brass pivot. The back is a solid brass underside. Golden brass with broad warm brown patina and sculpted cartoon highlights.
design.functional_surface_coverage: Front reveals the complete dial, glass and needle; the two opposite profiles reveal case thickness and the shallow glass protrusion; back reveals the full underside.
design.geometry_note: The lens is attached to the case. There is no lid, chain, mounting stand or extra prop. The compass rose is printed dial artwork; it is not a second movable needle.

reconstruction_pose.description: Upright on the circular edge, in exactly the same pose in all four views.

views.name: back

engine_resting_pose.description: Lying flat, with the dial facing upward.

reconstruction_to_engine.precondition: Verify the exported Tripo axes against the reconstruction coordinate convention. The following rotation applies only after those axes agree; do not blindly apply it to an unknown export orientation.

reconstruction_to_engine.placement_after_rotation: Recenter the X/Z bounds, put the lowest point at Y=0, then check the flat mesh against dimensions_m. The original edge-resting pivot will otherwise be offset.

generation_history.prompt:
Replace the compass turnaround in reference 1 with a genuinely useful 3D reconstruction sheet of ONE recognizable brass navigation compass. Reference 1 supplies only the brass case design, warm material and wear: its edge-on four views are the problem and MUST NOT be repeated. Reference 2 is the approved Captain Livé character turnaround: match its chunky sculpted cartoon game-art material language, soft simplified shaded forms, broad highlights and restrained worn edges. Do not include the character.

CRITICAL CHANGE — STAND THE COMPASS UPRIGHT ON ITS CIRCULAR EDGE in one fixed reconstruction pose in ALL FOUR VIEWS. The round dial is vertical, like a wall clock, but this is a small loose compass, NOT a clock, with no mounting, stand or supports. Its engine resting pose will be flat later. Keep the object upright; move only the orthographic camera around it. This exposes the entire upward-facing-in-game dial as the FRONT image.

Make exactly FOUR complete views in ONE horizontal row, LEFT TO RIGHT:
1 FRONT: a perfect face-on CIRCLE showing the full clear glass lens, cream/ivory dial, simple dark broad eight-point compass rose, clearly recognizable red north needle and pale white opposite south needle with a brass center pivot, surrounded by a substantial worn golden-brass bezel. North of the printed compass rose is at 12 o'clock; the red half of the needle points about 1 o'clock, the white half about 7 o'clock. Very subtle broad glass reflection that leaves the dial and needle readable. No giant glare. No clock numerals or clock hands.
2 LEFT SIDE: strict edge-on profile of the SAME upright disk. Projected width is exactly one THIRD of the circular diameter; projected height is exactly the full circular diameter. A narrow vertical brass casing silhouette. The raised glass/bezel lip is at the LEFT edge of this profile. No face-on dial visible.
3 RIGHT SIDE: opposite strict edge-on profile of the SAME upright disk, same height and thickness as view 2. The raised glass/bezel lip is at the RIGHT edge of this profile. No face-on dial visible.
4 BACK: full face-on circular underside, exactly same diameter as front, a solid brass backplate with simple broad bevel and a few chunky worn marks. No dial and no needle on the back.

PHYSICAL SHAPE: shallow, round compass, overall diameter 9 cm and full case thickness 3 cm. Upright reconstruction dimensions W9 × H9 × D3 cm. No lid, no chain, no hanging ring, no supports, no feet, no scenery, no other object. A broad brass bezel with simple case seam. Warm golden brass, brown tarnish restricted to seams and small broad edge chips; avoid photographic microdetail. Large clear functional shapes for a cartoony pirate adventure game.

CAMERA AND LAYOUT ARE NON-NEGOTIABLE: front, left, right, back are all straight-on LEVEL ORTHOGRAPHIC projections. Camera at the object's vertical midpoint, zero pitch and roll. No perspective, no three-quarter view, no tilted ellipses. Front and back are exact circles, not ellipses. All FOUR have the IDENTICAL pixel height, with outer top edges aligned to one common invisible top line and bottom edges aligned to one common invisible ground line. Orthographic scale must be identical: front/back full diameter, side profiles one-third as wide. Absolutely do not enlarge narrow side views to fill their cells. Use a wide panoramic white canvas with four evenly spaced view centers. Allow large completely blank white vertical bands separating every object; ample outer margins; no touching or overlapping. Use pure uniform opaque WHITE background everywhere outside the object, including all four corners. No floor, no cast shadow, no gradient, no vignette. No text, captions, view labels, dimensions, guides, arrows or callouts anywhere on the sheet. The printed rose and needle live only inside the actual compass face. One object per view, four images of the identical compass.

assembly.method: The repository cutter first places the generated views on equal native 683 px square canvases and aligns their bottoms. A subsequent user-authorized uniform affine transform reduces only the back view by 0.7339%, anchored at its horizontal centre and the shared ground line. The full fourth cell is resampled with Lanczos; the first three cells remain pixel-identical. See source.postprocessing_history for the exact transform and commands.
assembly.initial_command: python -B tools/crop_views.py <selected_raw_sheet> --out <temporary_crop_directory> --row 0 1 --names front left right back --pad 0.12 --size 683 --dry-run --preview art/props/compass/sheet.png

validation.method: Pixel foreground bounds measured against the modal background using tools/crop_views.py tolerance 18 (sum of RGB distance > 54), plus visual inspection of the functional surfaces and opposite profiles. These checks cover the sheet, not a reconstructed mesh.

review.recognizable_compass: Complete compass rose, one red/ivory needle, brass pivot, glass and bezel visible in the front.
review.surface_coverage: Dial in front, true narrow opposite edge profiles, complete underside at back.
review.projection: Level face-on circles and opposite edge profiles; no three-quarter panels.
review.profile_consistency: The shallow glass/bezel lip is on image-left in the left view and image-right in the right view.
review.isolation: Only the compass appears, with clear vertical background bands and no separate objects, labels or overlapping views.
review.completed_scale_check: After the user-authorized aspect-preserving back-view correction, front/left/right/back heights are 541/540/540/541 px. The maximum spread is 1 px, meeting the ART_SPEC raster tolerance. All four baselines are exactly y601. Front and back widths differ by only 1 px.

validation.compliance_scope: Final published sheet, including the expressly authorized precise scale correction. Raw generated-source measurements are preserved separately. This does not validate a reconstructed mesh or an engine import.

pipeline.upload_note: Match each crop to the corresponding named view in the reconstruction tool. Do not assume the sheet display order is the tool's positional upload order.
pipeline.lighting_note: The illustrated brass includes strong baked form and specular highlights. Use texture lighting removal where available and inspect the reconstructed material under engine lighting. Preserve the clear lens and readable dial.
pipeline.recommended_crop_command: python tools/crop_views.py art/props/compass/sheet.png --names front left right back --row 0 1 --size 1366 --out art/props/compass/views
pipeline.upscale_note: The published sheet uses native 683 px square cells. Export all crops at one common size; the recommended 1366 px output meets the documented minimum but adds no new detail. Preserve the corrected relative scale during extraction.
